**Security: pass-with-notes** at `880227b01abc6d7fce8d3677c0904798e09fee36`.

No new exploitable authority escalation, parser/shell injection or C19/C21 disclosure found. The new F-item release selector preserves #168's cutoff/pin and inherited any-seat release authority.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new scoped finding | - |

## What a crafted body can select

After GitHub reports the PR merged and a caller invokes `delivered`, `Fixes: F<N>` can select another coder's matching `coder/f<N>` holdings in the resolved project, if they began before the merge. It is not restricted to the PR author's seat or independently verified fixes. This is the documented any-seat release policy, not a new assignee-only permission bypass. Treat the body as an untrusted release selector, not proof the F-item is complete.

The additional F selector requires `held.role == "coder"` and an instance containing exactly lowercase `f` plus ASCII digits parsed as u64 (`crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:2103-2114,2294-2304`). A `security/f<N>` or other non-coder F holding cannot match it. The unchanged reviewer/security/performance holdings keyed by the PR can still end through the existing PR selector.

Selection excludes closed/end-pending/later/unparseable-time holdings. Targets retain exact `from`, and the writer checks it before ending a row, so same-key reassignment between selection and commit survives (`directory.rs:1979-1982,2114-2119`). The merge time remains from the requested PR's GitHub response, not its body. No unmerged PR alone causes a release.

## Parser and merge-check behavior

The shared Rust parser accepts case-insensitive/bulleted `Fixes:` heads, then only uppercase F plus nonempty ASCII digits within u64. Commas/whitespace separate values; surrounding backticks/asterisks are formatting; repeated values/lines are deduplicated. Signs, shell punctuation, nonnumeric suffixes and overflowing numbers cannot become selectors. Error lines/tokens are Debug-quoted, not executed (`crates/core/src/claims.rs:305-379`).

No matching line means no additional F-item release. A matching empty/malformed line returns `E-RS-FIXES` before recording delivery or changing holdings (`crates/daemon/src/http/claims.rs:364-397`).

The parser is line-oriented, not Markdown-aware: an actual matching line inside a fenced example or multiline HTML comment is still metadata. Review the raw body before running the merger command.

The pre-merge checker calls that same parser on stdin; the workflow passes the body in an environment variable with fixed-format quoted `printf`, never interpolates it into shell code (`crates/testkit/src/bin/delivers_check.rs:12-35`; `.github/workflows/delivers.yml:30-33`). Malformed metadata legitimately fails that PR's check and can be fixed or omitted. Body edits rerun its check; concurrency is keyed to the trusted PR ref, not body text. No new mechanism to block unrelated PRs or acquire merge authority was established.

The API retains the explicit F88/req-10 Known limit and any-seat policy (`docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:1797-1800`). Holding selection remains separate from authentication, ownership policy and completion proof. Existing Git/SQLite/window transaction and clock qualifications are not removed.

## Proof and limits

Local and GitHub heads agree; worktree clean; PR CLEAN and ready; all five checks succeeded. CI [42464104904](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42464104904) checked synthetic merge `4880e96`, incorporating this exact head. JUnit artifact [13611176783](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42464104904/artifacts/13611176783) has 2,237 passing cases with no failures, five separately skipped.

Confirmed executed: strict Fixes parsing; malformed/no-line/eligible/unnamed/later holding selection; controlled F-item release/reassignment pin; and the checker's valid/invalid Fixes cases. The actual Delivers job printed `Fixes: F122` and `Delivers: none`. Non-coder exclusion, overflow rejection and Markdown-line semantics were source-checked; no dedicated new regression for each was identified. Author-reported mutations were not independently rerun. ddocs was UNAVAILABLE.

Feature review plus dependent call sites, not an unrelated imported-main implementation review. No local cargo/builds/tests/scripts, credentials, actual release/delivery, product edits or production/pane/process probes.
